CHROMIUM: use delay_disconn_timer to avoid race conditions It is possible that a connected device may turn out to be disconnecting when the underlying shared library of bluez is still performing service discovery. Such race conditions result in 100-150 bluetoothd crashes in 24 hours when running the magic tethering test. Service discovery usually takes a few more seconds after device connection. However, upper-layer applications may request to disconnect the device before service discovery is completed. In this situation, it is possible that the GATT service related data structures that bluetoothd is trying to insert service data into may have been freed by the disconnection request. This would result in the following possible bluetoothd crashes when running Magic tethering test. The corresponding crash probabilities are also shown. c0: gatt_db_service_get_handles(): 52% c1: service_insert_characteristic(): 40% c2: notify_service_changed(): 4% c3: queue_isempty()/gatt_db_service_set_active(): 4% There are two possible methods to avoid the crashes. - Method 1: to add statements everywhere along the service discovery path to check if the device is disconnecting. The service discovery consists of a long chain of operations in the underlying shared library which are invoked sequentially and iteratively as callbacks and are difficult to stop. Hence, lots of such checking statements scattered everywhere should be added correctly in the code and thus would be difficult to maintain. - Method 2: add a delay for the device disconnection request if service discovery is still going on. The delay is tolerable and is not usually experienced by real users because a real user does not typically disconnect a device when it is just connected. It is supposed to be experienced only by upper-layer applications which perform continuous connection and disconnection very quickly. Method 2 is adopted in this patch. The device disconnection request is delayed at a 1-second increment up to a 10-second timeout when service discovery is still proceeding. The above maximal timeout is needed to avoid cases when service discovery is abnormally long or is stuck. In our testing, the following data show the probability and the time intervals within which the service discovery will be completed when the disconnection request comes in: <=1 seconds: 14% <=2 seconds: 45% <=3 seconds: 32% <=4 seconds: 7% <=5 seconds: 1% <=6,7,8,9,10 seconds: 0% >10 seconds: 1% It could be seen that 99% of the service discovery will be completed in 5 seconds%. And there is a 1% probability that the service discovery may take very long or even get stuck due to air noise or other reasons. BUG=chromium:911724 TEST=Use this patch and the other patch: - CHROMIUM: check if device is disconnecting during service discovery Perform Magic Tethering test for 24 hours. Verify that there are no bluetoothd crashes related with disconnection. Change-Id: Ia6ee08eb54be4bf9b34eb2bf5cfa03c83f4a99af Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1420426 Commit-Ready: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: check if device is disconnecting during service discovery It is possible that a connected device may turn out to be disconnecting when the underlying shared library of bluez is still performing service discovery. Such race conditions result in 100-150 bluetoothd crashes in 24 hours when running the magic tethering test. To fix the crashes, a device disconnecting flag is set in the lower-layer gatt-db structure. When performing service related queries, the flag and the service data structures are checked to avoid accessing those data structures that have been freed. This patch alone could reduce about 95% of the bluetoothd crashes caused by the race conditions between device disconnection and service discovery. This patch, when working together with the other patch, - CHROMIUM: use delay_disconn_timer to avoid race conditions resulting in no bluetoothd crashes caused by the mentioned race conditions. BUG=chromium:911724 TEST=Use this patch with the above patch. Perform Magic Tethering test for 24 hours. Verify that there are no bluetoothd crashes related with the mentioned race conditions. tast: Introduce the ephemeral devserver. When the tast command is run with -ephemeraldevserver=true (default) and no devserver specified, it starts a minimal devserver called ephemeral devserver. It listens on a TCP port on the DUT by SSH reverse forwarding, and proxies Google Cloud Storage requests with credentials installed on the host. This allows the DUT to access ACL'ed resources. bluetooth: base64 to encode/decode non-ASCII data When a DUT scanning devices nearby, it is possible that there are non-ASCII data in the device properties, e.g, ServiceData and ManufacturerData. While yaml is handy to serialize such data, yaml is unfortunately not available on some test server containers. It is possible to install yaml at the cost of extra size and installation time which is what we would like to avoid. Hence, it makes sense to work around using the built-in json module. The get_devices() is a list bluez dbus device objects. A recursive function is implemented as utils to apply base64 encode and decode methods on the device list. It calls recursively on sequences and dictionaries, and handles the basic types with the desired methods. Another culprit of json is that json cannot handle non-string keys in a dictionary. It converts for example a number into strings. We need to fix this culprit when applying base64 decoding method. Some debug messages has been added to print the data during encode/decode.
